summary: Markets are displaying a cautiously optimistic mood heading into a week dominated by U.S. midterm elections and high-profile earnings, with the FTSE 100 extending its winning streak to four consecutive sessions as oil prices ease on hopes of a U.S.-Iran diplomatic breakthrough. The midterm elections stand as the dominant macro catalyst, with prediction markets pricing a nearly 75% chance of Democrats retaining the Senate while sector rotations are already underway as investors position for potential policy shifts in energy, healthcare, and financials. At the stock level, Apple's post-bell earnings report is the single most-watched event, with options traders pricing in a significant move, while Kimberly-Clark's completed acquisition of Kenvue and CrowdStrike's fresh analyst upgrade are adding notable corporate newsflow; two major banks are also drawing attention for their roles at the center of large tech deal financing this week. The primary risk factors include unresolved Middle East tensions—highlighted by Houthi drone strikes toward Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport and continued Yemeni militant advances toward Aden—alongside Iran nuclear talks stalling without a breakthrough, which keeps geopolitical risk premiums elevated despite softer oil prices. In the short term, the combination of election outcome clarity, Apple earnings results, and any developments in U.S.-Iran negotiations will likely dictate near-term market direction, with historical S&P 500 patterns post-midterms generally supportive of equities once uncertainty lifts, though the VIX's unusual behavior signals investors remain on edge.
